key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term perovskite photoluminescence degradation from early time-series data, enabling faster stability prediction on unseen materials.
engineering_relevance: This could cut experimental screening time for perovskite solar-cell materials by reducing reliance on lengthy heat-and-light ageing tests while preserving interpretable stability insights.
method: Collected 86k+ photoluminescence spectra from 167 metal halide perovskites under elevated temperature and illumination.
Converted spectra into physics-informed features to encode degradation behavior and material descriptors.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM model to predict future PL intensity for samples not seen during training.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on a diverse 167-sample dataset and reportedly outperformed baseline benchmarks while generalizing across material groups.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of the physics-based featurization, so transfer to new compositions or measurement conditions should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
